summary: Remove 115/303, 309 from the reference list attached to nošo lo=qadər d-manəḥ ʕayne.
rationale: Both supplied verses have Gorgis as the revival patient and do not contain the quoted eye-healing sentence. Retain the other existing references; cite revival separately.

summary: Translate tawro as ox instead of cow
rationale: The Turoyo lu tawrayḏan refers to an ox, and the supplied edition translation at 44/95 explicitly reads Unser Ochse hat sich erholt. The supplied Ritter dictionary defines tawro as Stier, Ochse and cites 44/86 ff. Cow incorrectly makes the animal female.

summary: Correct both identifications of the animal: cow → ox
before: My uncle took off his pants and I wrapped them over it (the cow, m) little by little and God healed it (the cow, m) up
after: My uncle took off his pants and I wrapped them over it (the ox, m) little by little and God healed it (the ox, m) up
rationale: Both parenthetical identifications refer to the same ox. The edition at 44/113 says dem Ochsen; 44/94 explicitly identifies the animal as u tawro, and the supplied Ritter dictionary defines tawro as Stier, Ochse. Both occurrences of cow contradict this identification and the annotation m.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 2 in Infectum-wa (MAC Besim History of Bsorino/31)

data.turoyo: Omar, məd mašəġwa iḏe, marəswa am+maye ʕal ak+kayiwe, ʕal am+medone, noyáḥḥewa.
data.translation: It says, when he would wash his hands, he would sprinkle water on the sick people, on things, they would become healed.

rationale: New I Infectum-wa box, sense 2; habitual recovery with l-coded patients.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (57/176)

data.turoyo: w ʕayne kalən b sefe. D moyadwa, maḥatwalle b dukṯayye, gnayḥiwa, xəd meqəm.
data.translation: seine Augen liegen in seinem Schoß - wenn er sie nähme und an ihre Stelle legte, würden sie gesund werden wie zuvor.

rationale: New I Infectum-wa box, sense 1; hypothetical healing of plural eyes.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 1 in Infectum-wa (Jan 1.44/1881)

data.turoyo: Bəṯər mqafanwole darmone, qəsəm bam momo nayḥiwo, qəsəm bam momo mayṯiwo.
data.translation: Then they would prepare medicines for them; some would recover with those, and some would die with those.

rationale: Round 1 I.1 Infectum-wa has only an eyes example; this fills the cell with agreeing plural human subjects and a recovery/death contrast. It is not a new box. Supplied machine English.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (Jan 2.4/858)

data.turoyo: Hawxa ḥəmme gawonayto kəmmila. Msəkla i lašayḏi kula. Kmaškarno Aloho, bəṯər nayəḥwoli, aṯino lu bayto, šqiwoli darmone w mədone.
data.translation: An internal fever like this, they call it. It seized my whole body. I thank God; afterwards it eased for me. I came home; they bought me medicines and things.

rationale: First I Preterit-wa box: nayəḥ-wo-li with recovery context and l-coded experiencer. Machine English kept without replacing eased by a stronger cure translation.

summary: New box Preterit-wa: example for sense 2 in Preterit-wa (Jan 2.5/1275)

data.turoyo: Ǧan: Bəṯər u ḥasyo nayəḥwole?
data.translation: Jan: Afterwards the bishop recovered?

rationale: Second clear I Preterit-wa example in the new box, with an overt bishop topic and 3sg l-suffix; question supplies independent person contrast. Supplied machine English.

summary: New box Infectum-wa: example for sense 2 in Infectum-wa (Jan 2.13/3297)

data.turoyo: Mṣalewo aʕlayye, mu ṭaraf d Aloho nuyaḥwolle.
data.translation: He would pray over them; through God they would recover.

rationale: Fills I.2 Infectum-wa, already introduced in round 1; recovery follows repeated prayer and plural l-coded sufferers. Suffix segmentation remains a question; supplied machine English.

summary: New sense 2b: (unpersönlich mit l-) wieder lebendig werden, ins Leben zurückkehren

data.label: 2b
data.gloss: (unpersönlich mit l-) wieder lebendig werden, ins Leben zurückkehren

rationale: Two tellings describe children being washed for burial and then returning to life. This death-to-life event specialises recovery; not simply a new patient.

summary: New sense 1b: wieder lebendig machen, ins Leben zurückholen (auch einen Versteinerten)

data.label: 1b
data.gloss: wieder lebendig machen, ins Leben zurückholen (auch einen Versteinerten)

rationale: Explicit killing/restoration contrast at 67/215 and 230 corroborates medical revival at 67/207; 115/309 identifies Gorgis as a stone and specifies his return to life.

summary: example for sense 2 in Preterit Intransitive (JTM 5.1/40)

data.turoyo: məlla qum nayəḥlux!
data.translation: Sie sagte: Steh auf, du bist genesen!

rationale: Unusual 2sg l-coded recovery declaration with current result.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (MAC NE Mar Dumet/27)

data.turoyo: I+brusk̇e nayiḥo, i+brusk̇e nayiḥo. Eló balé ṣắqaṭyo, ṣắqaṭyo, komaʕraǧ bәḥḏo+raġlo.
data.translation: The pain got better, the pain got better. But he is lame, he is lame, he is limping on one leg.

rationale: Thin I.1 Preterit Intransitive cell; pain reduction explicitly contrasted with continuing lameness.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (PrS 45/24)

data.turoyo: Maḥatle bu fənǧan, maḥatle baʕ ʕayne du babo. Nayiḥi ʕayne du babo.
data.translation: dann goss er es in eine Tasse und legte es seinem Vater auf die Augen. Da wurden sie gesund.

rationale: Fills I.1 Preterit Intransitive to five; clear plural body-part subject.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (JTM 5.1/35)

data.turoyo: əmmo malle l aḥunux, u mede d səmle d umalle doġri, gənnaḥle w d l omər doġri u kewayḏe lə kuzze.
data.translation: Sie sagte: Sag deinem Bruder, wenn er ehrlich sagt, was er getan hat, dann wird er genesen. Wenn er es aber nicht ehrlich sagt, dann wird seine Krankheit nicht verschwinden.

rationale: Thin I.2 Infectum cell; recovery conditional on confession.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infectum (JTM 5.1/36)

data.turoyo: omər, aḥuno mar, mən d hawi mə d səmlux mare, yeter ki d nuyaḥlux!
data.translation: Er sagte: Bruder, sag, was auch passiert ist, was du auch getan hast, sag es! Hauptsache, du wirst gesund.

rationale: Fills I.2 Infectum to five; second-person l-coded desired recovery.

summary: example for sense 2 in Infinitiv (JTM 5.1/35)

data.turoyo: d məstaʕrəf bu kewayḏe, u mede d səmle gənnaḥle, w d lo, nyoḥo layto.
data.translation: Wenn er (den Grund für) seine Krankheit bekennt, das was er getan hat, wird er genesen, andernfalls gibt es keine Genesung.

rationale: Thin Infinitiv cell; recovery unavailable without confession.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 45/21)

data.turoyo: Duq u gelo w arṯeḥe b maye w kfaxe bu fənǧan w ḥete b ʕayne d babox, gnayḥi.
data.translation: Zerstosse das Gras und siede es in Wasser, dann giesse es in eine Tasse und lege es deinem Vater auf die Augen, so werden sie gesund werden;

rationale: Thin I.1 Infectum cell; plural eyes as recovering subject.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (PrS 66/65)

data.turoyo: Məllale li arnuwo əmmo: "D šotət ḥalwo, gnoyəḥ ṭizox."
data.translation: Nun hatte der Hase zum Fuchs gesagt: "Wenn du süsse Milch trinkst, so wird dein Hinterer gesund werden";

rationale: Thin I.1 Infectum cell; explicit singular body-part subject.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (57/30)

data.turoyo: Iḏa kan towelux gawre ṭawwe, d əzzən, mamtəlla u darmonawo, gnayḥi ʕaynux
data.translation: Wenn du tüchtige Männer hast, die hingehen und sie ..., das Heilmittel holen, so werden deine Augen gesund

rationale: Fills I.1 Infectum to five; explicit eyes and a complete treatment condition.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infinitiv (57/30)

data.turoyo: w lo, nyoḥo d ʕayne layt.
data.translation: wenn nicht, so gibt es keine Heilung für deine Augen.

rationale: First Infinitiv example for I.1; d-marked eyes as nominal patient.

summary: example for sense 2b in Preterit Intransitive (PrS 52/59)

data.turoyo: Mašəġila d qawrulle. Nayəḥḥe la tre bu šubḥo d Aloho.
data.translation: Darauf wusch sie sie, um sie zu begraben. Aber durch die Gnade Gottes kam den Beiden Leben zurück.

rationale: New I.2b revival subsense; burial preparation makes the death-to-life interpretation clear.

summary: example for sense 2b in Preterit Intransitive (PrS 52/103)

data.turoyo: Mašəġla ann abne d qawrulle, nayəḥḥe la tre w bu šubḥo d Aloho hawəlle quṣro harke.
data.translation: da wusch sie die Kinder, um sie zu begraben, aber sie kamen beide wieder in's Leben zurück, und durch die Gnade Gottes wurde ihnen hier ein Schloss,"

rationale: Second telling corroborates I.2b and retains the same l-coded frame.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JTM 4.3/10)

data.turoyo: omər ann abohoṯani lə ftəḥḥe ʕayn das samye, lə manəḥḥe aṣ ṣaqṭin, lə manəḥḥe ag garwone, lə manəḥḥe aš šaḥṭin, lə maqəmme miṯe?
data.translation: (Der Mönch) sagte: Haben diese Kirchenväter nicht die Augen der Blinden geöffnet, haben sie nicht die Lahmen geheilt, haben sie nicht die Aussätzigen geheilt, haben sie nicht die Krüppel geheilt, haben sie nicht Tote auferweckt?

rationale: Thin III Preterit cell; one context documents three coordinated patient classes.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit (JTM 5.1/40)

data.turoyo: manəḥla hawo stene,
data.translation: Sie heilte auch diesen.

rationale: Fills III Preterit to five; feminine healer and overt demonstrative patient.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (JTM 5.1/31)

data.turoyo: kit harke walaye rabṯo, kit biya dayroyo, kəmmi kmanəḥ ak kayiwe, gəmawbanne l tamo.
data.translation: dass es hier eine große Stadt gibt, in der ein Mönch ist, von dem man sagt, dass er die Kranken heilt. Dorthin werde ich ihn bringen.

rationale: Thin III Infectum cell; generic healing with explicit sick patients.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (78/164)

data.turoyo: Hayo gmaniḥoli w bas. Mede ḥreno lo komanəḥli.
data.translation: so wird das allein mich gesund machen. Nichts anderes kann mir Heilung verschaffen.

rationale: Fills III Infectum to five; inanimate remedial subject with first-person patient.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 34/94)

data.turoyo: Ummo: "De anəḥ. D manəḥatte, gxudmalləx šeṯ əšne."
data.translation: »Gut, heile sie«, entgegnete sie, »wenn du sie heilst, so will ich dir sechs Jahre dienen«.

rationale: Thin III Imperativ cell; reduced anəḥ.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 61/91)

data.turoyo: Qayəm azze l si zalḥafe, omər: "Aṯti kkoyawla, itəx aniḥa, d əbʕat, gdəbenəx."
data.translation: Jener begab sich zur Schildkröte und sagte: "Meine Frau ist krank geworden, komm und heile sie, was du willst, gebe ich dir."

rationale: Thin III Imperativ cell; singular patient suffix.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 61/93)

data.turoyo: Aṯən si tlawʕo. Omər: "Tlawʕo." Əmmo: "Ha." Omər: "Aṯti kkoyawla, aniḥulla hat w i zalḥafe, d əbʕat, gdəbenulxu."
data.translation: So kamen sie zum Wurme. "Wurm!" sagte er. "Ja!" "Meine Frau ist krank geworden, du und die Schildkröte sollt sie heilen; was du forderst, gebe ich euch."

rationale: Thin III Imperativ cell; two explicitly addressed healers.

summary: example for sense 1 in Imperativ (PrS 66/46)

data.turoyo: Aṯyo i kaftare l gabi, əmmo: "Anəḥ ʕayni."
data.translation: der Schakal kam zu mir und sagte: "Heile meine Augen.

rationale: Fills III Imperativ to five; overt eyes as patient.

summary: example for sense 1 in Infectum (3/27)

data.turoyo: Bas aġlab dam məskenani lə kmitaniḥi w kəmvayʕi ʕaynoṯayye.
data.translation: aber die Meisten dieser Armen Menschen sind unheilbar und verlieren ihr Augen(licht) (für immer).

rationale: Thin III Detransitive Infectum cell; negative curability context, cited but not printed in existing example.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infectum (67/207)

data.turoyo: Koṯe, kəmṭele lu bayto w kəmdarmən i lašayḏe w komoḥe darmono qum nḥire, komanəḥle.
data.translation: Er bringt ihn nach Hause, behandelt seine Leiche mit Arzneien, hält ihm Arzneien vor die Nase und macht ihn wieder lebendig.

rationale: New III.1b Infectum; treatment of a corpse followed by restoration, corroborated by killing contrasts at 215 and 230.

summary: example for sense 1b in Preterit (67/215)

data.turoyo: U kurrəko disa aṯi si pirayḏe. "Ha kurem, lə qṭilelux?" Omər: "Yade, qṭileli l aloho, manəḥleli.
data.translation: Der Junge kam wieder zu seiner alten." Nun, mein Junge, hat er dich nicht umgebracht?" "Er hat mich umgebracht, aber Gott hat mich wieder lebendig gemacht.

rationale: New III.1b Preterit; explicit killed versus restored contrast.

summary: example for sense 1b in Preterit (67/230)

data.turoyo: Məbloli naqla, qṭileli w ašər Ṭayre Simər l aloho w bəṯr ele manəḥleli w kaṯino u mərad, u maqṣadayḏi: kobaʕno, d mobanni i nxiraytayḏi."
data.translation: ich habe sie wiedergeholt, da hat er mich plötzlich getötet, aber Gott und dann der Vogel Simurgh haben mich wieder lebendig gemacht. Und nun bin ich gekommen und mein Begehr und Anliegen ist: ich will mir meine Braut wiederholen."

rationale: Thin III.1b Preterit cell; repeated explicit killing/restoration contrast.

summary: example for sense 1b in Infectum (115/303)

data.turoyo: gmanəḥ Gorgis naqla ḥreto,
data.translation: was Gorgis wieder lebendig machen kann.

rationale: Thin III.1b Infectum cell; Gorgis revival request, with petrification explained by supplied 115/309.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (Jan 2.33/5444)

data.turoyo: Yarḥo w falge-tre nayəḥli droʕi, hawi kayiso.
data.translation: A month and a half, two months, my arm healed; it became good.

rationale: Unusual direct body-part subject with an additional affected-possessor -li; retained despite a full cell because it tests the grammatical distinction between I.1 and I.2. Supplied machine English.

summary: example for sense 1 in Preterit Intransitive (Jan 3.21/497)

data.turoyo: Abgar məḥyole bi ḥurmayḏe w ban naʕimayḏe, b ruḥe hedi nayəḥ.
data.translation: Abgar applied it to his wife and to his children; he himself then recovered.

rationale: Clear human subject with suffixless nayəḥ contrasts with I.2 noyaḥ-lan and III maniḥ-at-lan in the same supplied episode; unusual argument pattern rather than thin-cell filler. Supplied machine English.

summary: Sense I.1 typically has an agreeing body-part or symptom subject (nayiḥi eyes; nayiḥo pain). I.2 uses an l-coded recovering person (nayəḥla, nayəḥlux), not an extra transitive healer. The inherited sense distinction is grammatical and must not be erased.

Assimilated nayəḥḥe and noyáḥḥewa obscure suffix number; edition plural pronouns alone cannot decide agreement. Infinitiv nyoḥo denotes recovery or its availability; nominal d- patient phrases do not carry finite agreement.
New Infectum-wa examples contrast habitual l-coded recovery at MAC Besim History of Bsorino/31 with hypothetical agreement on eyes at 57/176 and 70/271.

III Detransitive kmitaniḥi expresses possibility of cure; b ʕamaliye marks means, not a healer. 3/26 is already quoted; 3/27 is cited but its negative contrast is not printed, so one complementary context is supplied.

PrS 53/35 alone does not prove resurrection; its reader cites killings outside the supplied verse, so retain ordinary I.2 there. At 115/309 an alignment flag excludes every quotation of its supplied German.
All 27 supplied occurrences checked, including repeated tokens at 1.44/1878,2.13/3295 and 2.33/5443. Each has its own ordered decision; repeated tokens do not receive repeated examples.

Round 1 already fills ordinary I Preterit Intransitive/Infectum and III healing cells, and establishes I Infectum-wa. New evidence adds I Preterit-wa with l-coded recovery; no new sense or repeated revival proposal is needed.

Nayəḥ-li/le with an l-coded recovering person differs from III manəḥ-li/le with a healer agent. Jan 3.21/495 explicitly juxtaposes konoyaḥlan and maniḥatlan, while 497 supplies a direct human recovery subject.

The English at 3.21/494 says you heal the sick, although konoyaḥḥe lacks an overt 2sg ending and favors I recovery with plural l-coded sufferers. The example is withheld pending alignment/segmentation review; the English is not repaired or used to establish causative meaning.

The prayer over patients in 2.13/3297 is ordinary repeated recovery. No Jan token here independently establishes death-to-life I.2b or III.1b. Wanniḥ is explicitly Classical Syriac and excluded from Turoyo box proposals.
Confirm segmentation and number of nayəḥḥe, gnoyaḥḥe and noyáḥḥewa; distinguish assimilated l-suffixes from agreeing forms.
Is nayiḥi at PrS 32/11 Preterit Intransitive or an edition-specific Infectum vocalism? Withhold that example; clear parallels are available.
Resolve maniḥulle at PrS 78/82: III Preterit versus another form, and the reference of -ulle. Withhold quotation as a form exemplar.
Check printed gmaḥənnole at 24/58 against manəḥno-le; retain the source in decisions without silently correcting it.
At 78/203 is u mede towe ebe a subject or a supplementary description of the illness? The l-suffix favours I.2 provisionally.
Supply aligned German for 115/309 before any new example is quoted. The existing nyoḥo example is preserved, not retranslated.
Confirm literal death in the wider PrS 53/35 episode before extending 2b to it.
Jan 2.4/858,1050 and 2.5/1275: confirm the Preterit-wa temporal value; printed nayəḥ-wo-l- contrasts with Infectum nuyaḥ-wo-l-. The supplied English need not express anteriority overtly.
Jan 2.33/5444 nayəḥli droʕi: is -li an affected possessor with agreeing droʕi, or an impersonal experiencer with a body-part supplement? I.1 is provisional from the overt arm subject and hawi kayiso.

Jan 3.21/494 konoyaḥḥe and 2.13/3297 nuyaḥwolle: confirm plural experiencer suffix segmentation. Supply an independently aligned English gloss for 494 before publishing the machine causative translation as an I recovery example.
Jan 2.5/1587 gədnayḥi: are the recovering participants people or eyes? Either supports relief without necessarily full cure; do not create a new sense from that ambiguity.
A pain symptom can improve without full cure: MAC NE Mar Dumet/27 explicitly contrasts reduced pain with continuing lameness.
A remedial bowl can be the healing subject, retaining ordinary causative healing.

Personal recovery includes human subjects: qəsəm with plural nayḥiwo and Abgar b ruḥe with suffixless nayəḥ. The existing bodily/symptom exemplars do not restrict this sense to body parts; do not collapse it with l-coded I.2.

Prospective symptom relief mu kewo supports round 1's observation that improvement need not be complete cure. At 2.33/5444 droʕi co-occurs with -li, potentially an affected possessor rather than a second patient.
